title: Shared snapshots and per-language parser convergence

tests.name: test/parity/*.test.js
tests.detail: 4/4: snapshot-fed extraction equals stock disk extraction; prepared ingestion preserves the embedding input composition and reuses finalizeWrites; deletion, rename and definitionDelta rebind identically including cross-file incoming edges

findings: Convergence is enabled for javascript, typescript and python only, each backed by a passing parity test. Every other language keeps its existing extractor; the release gate fails if any language claims convergence without evidence.
Prepared ingestion reuses replaceFile/deleteFile/finalizeWrites and does not introduce a second durability point.
knownLimitations: Sixteen listed languages are not attempted. They are recorded as converged:false with a reason rather than assumed equivalent.
rollback: Point the extractors back at the disk-reading path; the snapshot input is additive.
